# steadycron_http_job (Resource)

Manages a SteadyCron HTTP job — a scheduled HTTPS call SteadyCron makes on your behalf.

Exactly one of `cron_expression` or `interval_seconds` must be set.

**Ownership note:** resources created via Terraform have a null `manifest_namespace`, so they are never pruned by `steadycron sync --prune`. Manage a resource via Terraform *or* the manifest/CLI, not both.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "steadycron_tag" "env_prod" {
  key   = "env"
  value = "prod"
  color = "green"
}

# HTTP job with a cron schedule
resource "steadycron_http_job" "weekly_digest" {
  name        = "weekly-digest"
  description = "Send the weekly digest email every Monday"

  method = "POST"
  url    = "https://api.example.com/jobs/digest"

  cron_expression = "0 9 * * 1" # Monday 09:00
  timezone        = "Europe/Berlin"

  timeout_seconds      = 120
  max_retries          = 2
  retry_backoff_seconds = 60

  headers = {
    Authorization = "Bearer {{digest_token}}" # server-side template substitution
    Content-Type  = "application/json"
  }

  body = jsonencode({ segment = "weekly" })

  skip_if_running = true

  tags = [steadycron_tag.env_prod.id]
}

# HTTP job with an interval schedule
resource "steadycron_http_job" "warm_cache" {
  name = "warm-cdn-cache"

  method           = "GET"
  url              = "https://api.example.com/warm"
  interval_seconds = 900 # every 15 minutes
}

output "weekly_digest_id" {
  value = steadycron_http_job.weekly_digest.id
}

output "weekly_digest_status" {
  value = steadycron_http_job.weekly_digest.status
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `method` (String) HTTP method. One of: `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`.
- `name` (String) Human-readable name for the job. In-place rename is supported without recreating the job.
- `url` (String) Target URL. Must be `http://` or `https://`. Private/RFC-1918 addresses are blocked by the SSRF guard.

### Optional

- `body` (String) Request body (for POST/PUT/PATCH).
- `cron_expression` (String) Cron expression (5-field). Mutually exclusive with `interval_seconds`.
- `description` (String) Optional free-text description.
- `headers` (Map of String) HTTP headers sent with each execution. Values containing `{{template_var}}` placeholders are resolved server-side at execution time.
- `interval_seconds` (Number) Run interval in seconds. Mutually exclusive with `cron_expression`.
- `key` (String) Stable job key referenced by code-monitoring SDKs.

When set, this exact string is used as the job key. When omitted, the server auto-generates a slug from the job name (visible after apply).

Changing `key` is an in-place update — no replacement occurs, but any in-code references using the old key must be updated. Must be unique within the account.
- `max_retries` (Number) Number of retry attempts on failure. Defaults to `0` (no retries).
- `misfire_policy` (String) What to do when a scheduled fire is missed (e.g. the scheduler was down). `do_nothing` skips the missed fire; `fire_once_now` executes once immediately. Defaults to `do_nothing`.
- `retry_backoff_seconds` (Number) Seconds to wait between retries. Defaults to `30`.
- `runbook_notes` (String) Markdown remediation notes shown inline in failure alert notifications (Slack, Telegram, Email). Max 4000 characters.
- `runbook_url` (String) Optional link to an external runbook (e.g. Notion, Confluence). Max 2048 characters.
- `skip_if_running` (Boolean) Skip the scheduled fire if a previous execution is still running. Defaults to `false`.
- `tags` (Set of String) Set of tag IDs to attach to this job. Use `steadycron_tag` resources and reference their `id`.
- `timeout_seconds` (Number) Request timeout in seconds. The server enforces a plan-specific maximum. Defaults to the account plan's default when not set.
- `timezone` (String) IANA timezone name for cron scheduling (e.g. `Europe/Berlin`). Defaults to `UTC`.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) RFC3339 creation timestamp.
- `id` (String) Server-assigned UUID for this job.
- `last_fire_at` (String) RFC3339 timestamp of the most recent fire.
- `next_fire_at` (String) RFC3339 timestamp of the next scheduled fire.
- `status` (String) Derived current status: `success`, `failure`, `running`, `paused`, `missed`, `skipped`, or `null` (new).
- `updated_at` (String) RFC3339 last-updated timestamp.
